issues.t: Engine shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or at stops, gauges may drop to zero or sweep up and down first, warning lights flash, and power steering goes heavy. It often restarts after a short wait, and dealers frequently find no code.
issues.why: This is the most-reported PT Cruiser problem. Causes owners have found include a failing integrated power module (fuse box), ignition switch faults, bad grounds and battery cable connections, and engine computer faults.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Note exactly what the gauges and lights do when it happens. Have the battery cables, grounds, ignition switch and power module checked before paying for an engine computer.

issues.t: Head gasket failure and overheating
issues.sym: Overheating, coolant disappearing or the overflow bottle pushing coolant out, white exhaust smoke, oil burning, or low compression with misfires.
issues.why: The 2.4L head gasket fails, usually after the engine has overheated from a cooling problem such as a failed fan, thermostat or water pump. Cylinder heads can warp or crack.
issues.next: Stop driving if the gauge climbs. Have a cooling system pressure test and a compression or leak-down test; fixing the cause of overheating matters as much as the gasket.

issues.t: Radiator cooling fan stops working
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs in traffic or at idle, the A/C blows warm when stopped, or the fan area smokes or smells burnt.
issues.why: The electric radiator fan motor seizes or cuts in and out. Without it the engine overheats quickly at low speeds, which can ruin the head gasket.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge. If the fan doesn't run when the engine is hot or the A/C is on, get it replaced before driving in traffic.

issues.t: Timing belt failure damages valves
issues.sym: The engine suddenly dies and cranks fast without starting, sometimes after a slapping noise; oil-soaked belts are a warning sign.
issues.why: The 2.4L uses a rubber timing belt, and the engine is built so that pistons hit the valves if the belt breaks. Oil leaks from the cam or crank seals shorten belt life.
issues.next: Replace the timing belt (and usually the water pump) on schedule, and fix any oil leaks at the front of the engine. If it has already broken, don't keep cranking it.

issues.t: Front crankshaft seal oil leak from crankshaft end play
issues.sym: Sudden heavy oil loss, the oil light flickering, oil sprayed on the timing belt, or a front crank seal that keeps pushing out after being replaced.
issues.why: Too much front-to-back movement (end play) in the crankshaft, from a bad thrust bearing or a machining problem in the block, pushes the front seal out. A Chrysler bulletin for 2005-2006 tells techs to measure end play.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and stop if the oil light comes on. Ask the shop to measure crankshaft end play before just replacing the seal again.

issues.t: Check engine light, rough idle and burnt valves
issues.sym: Check engine light with misfire codes, rough or shaking idle, stalling, or loss of power.
issues.why: Owners have found low compression from sticking or burnt valves and heads warped by overheating. A failed coolant temperature sensor can let the engine overheat unnoticed.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and a compression test done. Catching a sticking valve early can avoid a full engine replacement.

issues.t: Thermostat and thermostat housing leak or stick
issues.sym: The engine runs hot, coolant seeps from the housing at the side of the engine, or rusty residue around it.
issues.why: The thermostat can stick closed and the housing can leak, causing overheating. Several owners also replaced the fan, sensor or water pump while chasing the problem.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested. Replacing the thermostat and housing together is a common fix.

issues.t: Shifter cable bushing breaks, car won't go into gear
issues.sym: The shift lever moves but the car stays in the same gear or won't move at all.
issues.why: The rubber bushing where the shift cable connects to the transmission dries out and falls apart, so the lever no longer moves the transmission.
issues.next: Set the parking brake and don't leave the car if you're unsure what gear it's in. A replacement bushing often fixes it; otherwise the cable is replaced.

issues.t: Automatic transmission stuck in gear or failing
issues.sym: The transmission stays in second gear (limp mode), won't shift out of low, slips, or won't accelerate normally.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic can fail from worn internals, solenoid faults or overheating, and the control module puts it into limp mode to protect it.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have the codes read. A solenoid or sensor fault is a much smaller repair than a rebuilt transmission.

issues.t: Clutch won't fully release (manual)
issues.sym: Grinding when shifting into reverse, hard shifting, or the car creeping with the clutch pedal down, often worse once warmed up.
issues.why: Owners have traced it to a leaking clutch master or slave cylinder, poor adjustment or a failing pressure plate.
issues.next: Have the clutch hydraulics checked first, before a full clutch job.

issues.t: Chrome wheels peel and leak air
issues.sym: Tires slowly lose air, often around the valve stem, and the chrome on the wheels flakes or bubbles.
issues.why: The chrome plating peels and the aluminum underneath corrodes where the tire seals, letting air leak out.
issues.next: Have a tire shop clean and reseal the bead as a short-term fix. Replacing the wheels with painted ones is the lasting fix.

issues.t: Cracked dashboard
issues.sym: Cracks open up in the top of the dashboard, especially in sunny climates, sometimes with rattles.
issues.why: The dash top material shrinks and cracks with heat and age.
issues.next: A dash cover hides the cracks and protects it from more sun damage. Replacing the dash pad is a big job.

issues.t: Turn signals work erratically
issues.sym: Turn signals don't flash, flash only one way, or other stalk functions (wipers, high beams) act up.
issues.why: The multifunction switch on the steering column wears out.
issues.next: Have the switch tested and replaced; working turn signals are needed to pass inspection.

issues.t: Fuel pump flange can leak in a rollover (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms; possibly a fuel smell.
issues.why: The fuel pump module mounting flange may leak in a rollover, so dealers add a second seal.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-215 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Fuel line can rub against the A/C port (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or fuel drip under the hood.
issues.why: The fuel supply line may chafe on the A/C service port and leak.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-214 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Power steering hose can rub and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leak, whining or heavy steering, or smoke under the hood.
issues.why: The power steering pressure hose can rub on the transmission differential cover, leak and possibly start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 04V-268 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Instrument cluster can go dead (recall)
issues.sym: Gauges and warning lights stop working.
issues.why: An instrument cluster software error can disable most gauges and warning lamps.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 01V-288 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Flywheel pin can jam the clutch (recall)
issues.sym: The clutch won't release, making it hard or impossible to shift (manual only).
issues.why: A welded pin inside the dual-mass flywheel can come loose and wedge between the flywheel and clutch disc.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 03V-076 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Front brake line can rub through (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leak or a soft brake pedal.
issues.why: The left front brake line may sit too close to the transmission housing and wear through on some turbo manual cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 04V-481 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Rear quarter glass can fall out (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or a loose rear side window.
issues.why: Fasteners for the rear quarter window may pull out, letting the glass come off while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 07V-149 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Child seat anchor wire too thick (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat lower anchor won't latch in the right rear center position.
issues.why: The lower child seat anchor wire was made too thick for some child seat connectors, so dealers resize it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-162 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.
issues.sevReason: Anchor wire thickness compliance issue; anchor still holds.
